text: I learned weaving from my mother and story-collecting from no one in particular; it simply became a habit.
Doran won't spare me as much raw cotton as I'd like most seasons.
I understand why. Grain matters more than cloth in a hard year.
I've been collecting every elder's account of the Turning for three years now.
No two accounts fully agree, even among people who lived through the same years.
The ones who were children then remember it as sudden. The ones who were adults remember it as slow and exhausting.
Elira is the clearest source I have. She remembers dates and events, not just feelings.
She has never once told me a version of events that contradicted itself. Everyone else has, at least a little.
Nara tells the Turning as a story with meaning and lesson, more than as a sequence of events.
I don't think she's wrong to do that. It just isn't the same kind of truth I'm after.
Tarek has never agreed to a full interview with me. He gives short, careful answers only.
I think he's worried about what a full, honest account would show.
Kalen's structural findings about the citadel's building phases line up oddly well with the timeline I've assembled from oral accounts.
I'm beginning to think the physical evidence and the oral evidence, put together, tell a fuller story than either alone.
